Title: Passage 3: Icarus After the Fall
Content: The waves slapped Icarus in the face,
a salty sting to his ego.
He had soared so high, he scraped sky blue on his tunic before
SPLASH.
He had been having a time peering down on everyone from above,
until his waxed wings began to melt,
and he dropped like a stone,
feathers fluttering behind him,
the ocean spread out below like a mirror.
He caught his reflection a moment before he shattered the surface —
eyes bulging,
hair tangled,
forehead bare.
Not exactly a picture for the history books.
He treaded water, wondering how in the world he would spin this to old Daedalus.
I was flying so well, a wind gust caught me, and, and it pushed me up
or better yet
I saw a dangerous eagle diving towards you, and, and I vanquished it!
A disastrous weakness becomes a noble tale.
Would it work? Probably not —
though it might make a decent story to tell his friends.
He plucked at the scattered wax and feathers,
little bobbing bits of his broken pride.
I need to get to shore.
The man who’d touched the atmosphere had no choice but to swim.
It was then that he heard a voice just behind him,
“Excuse me, sir, do you need a hand?”
A wizened, weathered fisherman in a simple rowboat reached out to help.
Icarus blinked a moment and spat a mouthful of ocean
(his fabled smile perfect but not watertight).
“A hand? I don’t need any help! Did you not see? I was flying!”
